entries.template: From {totalObjects} students, a committee of {selectedObjects} is to be formed and one committee member is to be appointed chairperson. In how many ways can this be done?

From {totalObjects} players, a team of {selectedObjects} is selected. A captain and a vice-captain are then appointed from the selected team. In how many ways can the complete selection and appointment be made?

A committee of {selectedObjects} is chosen from {totalObjects} members. The posts of chairperson, secretary and treasurer are then assigned to three different committee members. Find the number of possible outcomes.

From {totalObjects} contestants, {selectedObjects} finalists are shortlisted. Among the finalists, {roleCount} distinct ranks are awarded. In how many ways can the shortlist and ranked awards be decided?
From {totalObjects} distinct books, {selectedObjects} books are chosen and all the chosen books are arranged in a row. How many outcomes are possible?
From {totalObjects} speakers, {selectedObjects} are chosen and assigned to {selectedObjects} numbered presentation slots, one speaker per slot. In how many ways can this be done?

After a group of {selectedObjects} people has been selected, {roleCount} distinct offices are assigned to different members of that group. By what factor does the office assignment multiply the selection-only count?

A group of {selectedObjects} is chosen from n people and then {roleCount} distinct offices are assigned to different selected members. If the total number of outcomes is {target}, find n, where {minimumTotalObjects} ≤ n ≤ {maximumTotalObjects}.

From {totalObjects} people, a group of s is chosen and then {roleCount} distinct offices are assigned to different selected members. If the total number of outcomes is {target}, find s, where {minimumSelectedObjects} ≤ s ≤ {maximumSelectedObjects}.

A group of {selectedObjects} is chosen from {totalObjects} people and then k distinct offices are assigned to different selected members. If the total number of outcomes is {target}, find k, where 1 ≤ k ≤ {maximumRoleCount}.
